message: Hi John, yes I have a boom arm that can get a 90 degree top-down angle, and soft box to diffuse the lighting... Thanks again, let me know if you have any other questions...

Great, thanks for confirming you have the boom arm and softbox.

I’ll send over the shot list and the technical requirements for the tabletop video walkthrough. This will outline the overhead 90° setup, lighting, and the short video walk‑through while the piece is displayed. For the documentation, I need to video the three panels individually, and also the three together while they are displayed on the same black velvet tabletop used for the shoot. ( I have the velvet and table). The clips need to be edited together to produce a single 20-40 sec video. Its straightforward. I'm attaching the shot list document for added detail and clairty.

Let me know if you have questions, and we can discuss.
Great, let me study over tonight and get back in the morning with any questions. Thanks John!
Question... How tall is the table top, and the high are the ceilings?...
Table height is 29 inches, and ceiling height is 8 ft.”

Added Note: I have a collapsible table that can be used, which can bring the height down to 2 inches off the floor. This will give the flat surface necessary to cover with the black velvet, and plenty of overhead room to comfortably take shots and shoot the video. As long as the boom arm off the tripod locks at 90 degrees it will work well. Ideally the art would be wall mounted for shoot, but since the documentation will take place on tabletop there is the necessity to keep 90 degrees so that the shots are square.

Hello John, Thanks for the info... The shorter table will be better option so we can get the light angled where we need it, but let's keep the taller table available in case we need it. Reviewing your shot list, it's something I can produce. Last question, can I also get the sizes of the each panel?... Thank you in advance!

Three physical panels: 8x10 inches each. It's a triptych.

Let me know if you need anything else for planning the lighting and framing.
Sounds good, yeah I think we got it! I'm available next week, Wednesday-Friday, Ideally morning, Starting at 10am... With set-up and tear down, we should be done before 1pm, the latest 2pm...

Wednesday at 10am works. Let’s lock that.

Setup, shoot, and teardown within your 10am–2pm window is fine. I’ll have the panels, velvet, and both table options ready.

I’ll draft the contract and send it to you tomorrow morning.
Roger that!
